'''Antonio Luiz Braga''' was born in [[Herculândia]], Brazil.

He graduated with a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[chemistry]] from the [[Federal University of São Carlos]] in 1981, [[master's degree]] in [[Organic chemistry|Organic Chemistry]] from the [[University of São Paulo]] in 1984, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Organic Chemistry from the University of São Paulo in 1989 under the guidance of Professor Comasseto.

He was Professor of Chemistry at the [[Federal University of Santa Maria]] (1985-2008). He was coordinator of the Chemistry Committee of FAPERGS (2000-2001). He was coordinator of a Center of Excellence project (PRONEX-2005 -.. Support Center for Bio-Organic Organocalcogênios, He was General secretary of the 11th Brazilian Meeting on Organic Synthesis (11th BMOS, 2005). Currently,{{when|date=September 2022}} he is a professor at the [[Federal University of Santa Catarina]], Chemistry Department.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://ppgqmc.posgrad.ufsc.br/braga/ | title=PPGQ}}</ref> He has experience in Organic synthesis, acting on the following topics: [[Green chemistry|Green Chemistry]], [[Asymmetric catalysis|Asymmetric Catalysis]], [[Organoselenium chemistry|organoselenium]] bioactive molecules and [[selenium]] and [[tellurium]] derived [[amino acid]]s and other natural products, Synthesis of the seleno-enzyme glutathione peroxidase mimetic.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1002/slct.201702623|title = Fe3 O4 Nanoparticles: A Robust and Magnetically Recoverable Catalyst for Direct C-H Bond Selenylation and Sulfenylation of Benzothiazoles| journal=ChemistrySelect| volume=3| pages=328–334|year = 2018|last1 = Rafique|first1 = Jamal| last2=Saba| first2=Sumbal| last3=Frizon| first3=Tiago E. A.| last4=Braga| first4=Antonio L.}}</ref> Coordinates CT_Infra projects at UFSC; published over 340 papers in journals recognized by the community, cited by 15115 research articles, H level:.. 66, deposited 8 patents (USA, Brazil). Award: researcher Featured in Chemistry, FAPERGS, 2007; Santa Catarina Outstanding Researcher-Fritz Muller Award (FAPESC, 2023) and  BMOS Award, 2024.

In 2009, he was elected member in the advisory board of the International Conference on the Chemistry of Selenium and Tellurium (ICCST). A member of the CNPq Chemistry Committee between 2009 - 2011 (CA Coordinator between 2009 and 2010). Designated and elected member of the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]] (ABC).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.abc.org.br/resultadoPT.php3?codigo=braga |title=Academia Brasileira de Ciências |access-date=2016-09-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170717223600/http://abc.org.br/resultadoPT.php3?codigo=braga |archive-date=2017-07-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2014, he was elected to the advisory board of the Brazilian Chemical Society (SBQ).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://buscatextual.cnpq.br/buscatextual/visualizacv.do?metodo=apresentar&id=K4788861Z7 |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=buscatextual.cnpq.br|title=Busca Textual - Currículo Lattes}}</ref>
